2026-12-14.title: Monday of the Third Week of Advent · St John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor
readings: A star shall come out of Jacob
Teach me your ways, O Lord
By what authority are you doing these things?
2026-12-14.alt: Memorial of St John of the Cross, priest and doctor of the Church.
2026-12-14.verse: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near—a star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel.
theo: Balaam was a pagan seer hired to curse Israel, but the Spirit of God came upon him and he could only bless. He sees from afar: “a star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel.” The Fathers saw this fulfilled in the star the Magi followed to Bethlehem. God can speak truth even through unexpected mouths.

In the Temple the chief priests challenge Jesus: “By what authority are you doing these things?” He answers with a question about John's baptism: from heaven or human? They calculate and refuse to answer. Truth requires honesty; the leaders preferred safety. St John of the Cross, the Carmelite mystic, wrote that we must pass through the “dark night” of purification to reach union with God, and: “In the evening of life, we will be examined in love.”
outline: Ask: how do you respond when God's truth is inconvenient?
Christ's authority comes from the Father.
live: Face one truth about yourself you have been avoiding.
Pray in the dark (St John of the Cross)
Spend ten minutes in silent prayer, even if you feel nothing.
2026-12-14.prayer: Lord, star rising from Jacob, teach me your ways. Give me an honest heart that does not calculate but obeys, and lead me, like St John of the Cross, through every dark night to union with you. Amen.
altar: At Mass the Star of Jacob comes near. We no longer see him only from afar; we receive him.

quick: God's star rises even through an unexpected prophet.
Truth asks for honesty, not calculation.
2026-12-14.action: Spend ten minutes in silent prayer.
2026-12-14.question: Which truth am I avoiding?

family.explain: Long ago a man saw a vision of a star that would come from Jacob. Christians believe this star is Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who are searching for God.
family.ask: Ask: “Are we brave enough to say we love Jesus, even when it is not easy?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Star of Jacob, you shine on all who seek you. As we gather, free us from calculation and fear, and give us honest hearts. Amen.
share: Balaam saw the star from afar (Numbers 24:17). How has Christ come near to me?
The leaders said: we do not know (Matthew 21:27). When do I avoid the truth because it is inconvenient?
What would it mean for me to give everything, like St John of the Cross?
pm.resp: Lord, let your light shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may speak the truth with courage.
For those who seek God sincerely, that the Star may guide them.
For contemplatives and Carmelites, through the prayers of St John of the Cross.
For leaders, that they may seek truth rather than popularity.
For our group, that we may be honest in our faith.
pm.close: Lord God, you showed Balaam the star from afar. Let your Son, the bright morning star, rise in our hearts, and give us courage to follow the truth. Amen.

illus: A college student in Chennai was asked by friends whether she really believed in God. She was tempted to joke and avoid the question. Instead she said simply: “Yes, I do, and it has changed my life.” Two of them later asked her to take them to church.

homily: Dear friends, in the first reading a pagan prophet, Balaam, is hired by a king to curse Israel. Instead, the Spirit of God comes upon him and he blesses them. He sees from afar: a star shall come out of Jacob, and a sceptre shall rise out of Israel (Numbers 24:17). God can speak even through unexpected people.

The Church has always seen in this star a prophecy of Christ, and of the star that led the Magi to Bethlehem. Balaam saw him, but not now; beheld him, but not near. We, who have seen him come near, are more blessed.

In the Gospel the chief priests and elders challenge Jesus: by what authority are you doing these things? Jesus answers with a question: did the baptism of John come from heaven, or was it of human origin? They reason: if we say from heaven, he will ask why we did not believe; if we say of human origin, we fear the crowd. So they answer: we do not know (Matthew 21:23–27).
They were not really seeking the truth; they were calculating. Their answer depended on what was safe, not on what was true. Jesus would not play their game.

Today we remember St John of the Cross, who was imprisoned by his own brothers for seeking reform, yet in his dark cell wrote some of the most beautiful poems of love for God. He did not calculate; he gave everything.

Do I sometimes calculate in matters of faith? I will speak about God only if it is safe; I will go to Mass if there is nothing better to do; I will forgive if they apologise first. This Advent let us seek the truth honestly and follow it, like the star of Jacob, wherever it leads. Amen.
kids: Children, a star led the wise men to Jesus. Ask Jesus to be the bright star that guides you every day!

intro: Theme: “A star shall come out of Jacob.”
God's promise shines from afar; Christ's authority is from heaven; truth asks for honesty.

sub: Balaam came to curse and blessed.
He saw the star from afar.
q: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near—a star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel; it shall crush the borderlands of Moab, and the territory of all the Shethites.
Asking, “Where is the child who has been born king of the Jews? For we observed his star at its rising, and have come to pay him homage.”
points.apply: Put up your Christmas star with a prayer.

sub: His authority is from the Father.
He teaches as no one else.
q: Make me to know your ways, O LORD; teach me your paths. Lead me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation; for you I wait all day long.
When he entered the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority?”
points.apply: Let Christ's word have authority in one decision.

q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Did the baptism of John come from heaven, or was it of human origin? And they argued with one another, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’”
points.apply: Face one truth you have avoided.

concl: The star is rising; answer honestly.
In the evening of life we will be judged on love.
2026-12-14.resolve: Make a quiet holy hour this week.
